newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MCDERMOTT DEDICATES NEWCASTLE DISPLAY TO KEEGAN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MCDERMOTT DEDICATES NEWCASTLE DISPLAY TO KEEGAN.

text.p: Rarely can anyone not involved in any of the action so dominate the thoughts of thousands of people on a Saturday afternoon during the English soccer season.
Kevin Keegan, who walked out as Newcastle manager on Wednesday, was obviously nowhere to be seen at Villa Park on Saturday where the team he created drew 2-2 in a thrilling match with Aston Villa.

He was believed to be in Marbella, where he spent most of his eight-year retirement from the game in the 1980s, but his influence was everywhere -- especially in the way Newcastle flattered to deceive yet again.

They rushed into a 2-0 lead after only 21 minutes with goals from Alan Shearer and Lee Clark, and then threw the victory away by conceding two soft goals after dreadful defending which allowed Dwight Yorke and Savo Milosevic to pull the game around for the home side.
Only a save by Shaka Hislop midway through the second half from a poorly-taken penalty by Yorke saved Newcastle from defeat.
Much of the media coverage of Keegan's departure echoed that which follows the deaths of the great and the grieved.
But while Keegan's departure stunned soccer-crazy Geordie fans and left them crying tears of despair into the River Tyne, there are other questions that need to be asked.
Why did a manager who spent 60 million pounds ($100 million) on his side not manage to win one single trophy or take that side into the semifinals of a single cup competition?
And why wasn't any of the vast amount of money made available by chairman Sir John Hall spent on strengthening the defence which caved in under the pressure of chasing the title last season?
It was left to Keegan's assistant Terry McDermott and former Newcastle manager Arthur Cox to start answering the questions Keegan ultimately failed to address.
Caretaker manager McDermott said he would be delighted to continue in the job, but also said that whoever the club eventually appointed would be the right man.
The team he and Cox put out on Saturday had no surprises and played in the way Newcastle teams have played for most of the last five years under Keegan.

But whoever takes long-term control of the team must bring some organisation to the defence. Without a decent one, no team has ever won the title and this Newcastle team are unlikely to prove an exception.
McDermott said afterwards: "That result was for Kevin" and he added that Keegan -- wherever he was -- would have been proud of his former side's display.
"I would like to think he watched that as I know it has been beamed around Europe and I am sure he would have been proud of that.
"That result was for Kevin, he would want us to play that way."
And McDermott was quick to point out that Newcastle would continue to play in Keegan's style.
He added: "We just want to entertain and win trophies, that is very important. There won't be a lot of change in the way we play: we score, you score.

"We are quite capable of winning the championship make no mistake about that. If you look at the results today you can see that any team in the League can beat any other. The bottom side can beat the top."

McDermott was full of praise for the way his side handled the aftermath of Keegan's departure and admitted: "It was a very emotional day. I thought the lads were tremendous after all the turmoil of the last three or four days. To produce a performance like that was excellent.
"They were aware that the spotlight was on them but they did Newcastle proud as you never know how players are going to react.
"When I told them (about Keegan's departure) on Wednesday there were a lot of grey faces which was understandable."
A thousand reasons have been put forward for Keegan's exit, the timing of which was more surprising in many ways than the fact that he left.

Much of the speculation has centered on the way Newcastle blew their 12-point lead in the title run-in last season, allowing United to overhaul them in the final weeks to finish not only as champions, but Cup and League double winners for the second time in three seasons.

If that was the main cause of his departure then there was some other news for him on Saturday that might have turned a few Bookmakers William Hill installed United as favourites to win the title again. Manchester United, not Newcastle United. But luckily, Keegan doesn't have to get stressed by that sort of thing now.
